reviewed_tree: e6f678441 plus the uncommitted link-fallback fix that the commit after it adds (TaskLinkRejectedError; engine retries unlinked only on TASK_LINK_REJECTED)
method: Read-only claude -p run (Read, Grep, Glob, git diff/show/log only; no builds or tests), whole branch diff origin/main...HEAD plus the working-tree diff. Raw output: session scratchpad 208-stoa-security.out.

supersedes.note: Local pre-squash commit; its full verdict is in git history of this file. Superseded because the 2026-10-29 security-relevant commits (1d5758f9d, e6f678441) and the link-fallback fix landed after it.

checks.name: secret-shaped strings in added lines (postgres://user:pass@, Bearer, sk-, ghp_, AKIA, JWT, private keys, *.supabase.co, *.neon.tech)
checks.evidence: Ran `git diff origin/main...HEAD -G <pattern set>`. The only file it returned is .specify/sprints/sprint-18/execution/PG-208/20261020231931-3d9aa8b9/matop/stoa-verdicts/security.json, which names the patterns in prose and contains no secret values. Ran `git diff -G` on the uncommitted tree: the hits are the substring 'sk-' inside 'task-automation-...' identifiers in the two test files, not secrets. Grep with the full pattern set over apps/api/src/modules/task returned 0 matches. .gitleaks.toml:61-62 and the second allowlist (lines ~73-77) only add the PG-208 attestation JSON paths, which are generated hash maps scoped to existing rule allowlists. .env.example adds only TASK_AUTOMATION_INTERVAL_MS=15000. Test tokens are built at runtime with 'tat_' + randomBytes(32) (http-server.task-automation-webhook.test.ts, task-automation-webhook.test.ts).

checks.name: webhook HMAC signing and constant-time compare
checks.evidence: task-automation-webhook.ts:122-132 is HMAC-SHA256 over `${t}.${idempotencyKey}.` + raw body bytes. :134-138 compares with timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers. :36 has a strict SIGNATURE_PATTERN (10-digit t, 64 hex chars) and :151-153 rejects malformed input before any compare. :158-164 allows the previous secret only while webhookSecretPreviousExpiresAt > now.

checks.name: replay window and idempotency
checks.evidence: webhook.ts:155-157 enforces the skew window against L.webhookSkewSeconds. The Idempotency-Key is inside the signed string (:129), so a replay cannot change the key. store.ts:311-315 looks up the existing run by the (ruleId, idempotencyKey) unique pair inside the admission transaction. webhook.ts:302-305 returns 202 duplicate when payloadHash matches and 409 idempotency_conflict when it differs.

checks.name: token storage (hash only) and tenant isolation of the token lookup
checks.evidence: task-automation.router.ts:89 makes the token from 32 random bytes. :778-779 store only sha256Hex(token) plus a display prefix. The plaintext is returned once (:791, :979). RULE_SELECT (:156-182) omits the hash and secrets. store.ts:702-717 does loadWebhookRule with findUnique on the globally unique webhookTokenHash; tenantId comes from the matched row and drives settings and admission. Under the lock, store.ts:316-331 re-reads with the tenant-scoped FOR SHARE (:291-295) and webhook.ts:288-290 re-verifies the token hash and signature against the locked credentials.

checks.name: webhook failure limiter (per IP and per IP+token hash, before lookup and body read); cross-tenant throttling
checks.evidence: Route webhook.ts:389-398 checks the bare-IP bucket and, for a well-formed token, the ip|sha256(token) bucket before the content-length check and the bounded body read (:404-415). Handler :246-248 checks the rule key before store.loadWebhookRule. Unknown tokens count against the bare IP (:251). Inactive, disabled and bad-signature failures on a real rule count only against ruleKey (:252,254,258), so one tenant's failing sender no longer fills the shared IP bucket. Test http-server.task-automation-webhook.test.ts (+29 lines in e6f678441) shows tenant-b gets 202 from the same IP and the throttled token gets 429 without any lookup. Map is bounded by MAX_TRACKED_IPS with expired-first eviction (:40, :70-91). Residual bare-IP sharing for unknown tokens is the accepted PG-208-WEBHOOK-UNKNOWN-TOKEN-IP-BUCKET-001.

checks.name: uniform error responses with no leaks
checks.evidence: webhook.ts:48-50 defines constant bodies. Unknown, inactive or disabled tokens all get NOT_FOUND (:244,251,252,254,296). Every signature or key failure gets the same 401 (:258). The route catch (:417-421) logs only err.name and returns a generic {error:'internal'}. The test 'returns a generic 500 ... without the error message' is present. Router RULE_SELECT and listRuns select (:731-740) expose no secrets.

checks.name: body size and time limits
checks.evidence: webhook.ts:404-408 pre-checks content-length against L.webhookBodyMaxBytes. readBoundedBody (:318-347) stops buffering past maxBytes and applies a 10 s BODY_READ_TIMEOUT_MS (:39). sendAndClose (:363-368) discards the rest of the upload and destroys the socket after 2 s. Read failures count against the IP (:400-403).

checks.name: secret encryption at rest and rotation/regeneration under the row lock
checks.evidence: webhookEncryptionReady (webhook.ts:111-114) and the 503 fail-closed at :255. assertWebhookEncryptionReady is called in create (router:751) and rotate (:932). rotateWebhookSecret (router:938-957) runs inside $transaction with lockTenantRules and reads the current secret under the lock (keepPrevious :945-953), so concurrent rotations cannot bring back a revoked secret. regenerateWebhookUrl (:970-976) is a single atomic tenant-scoped updateMany, and admission re-checks credentials.webhookTokenHash === tokenHash under FOR SHARE (store.ts:316-331, webhook.ts:288-290), so a request using an old URL loses to a committed regeneration. The tick's clearExpiredPreviousSecrets (store.ts:680-686) is not needed for correctness, because verifySignature checks expiry itself.

checks.name: RBAC on the taskAutomation router (admin gates, audited denials) and on manager UI controls
checks.evidence: task-automation-admin.ts:29-56 gives assertTaskAutomationAdmin a webhook scope narrower than rules (no MANAGER) and audit-logs every denial through logPermissionDenied before FORBIDDEN. Write paths: settings.update :547, tags.* :608/635/671, listRuns :725, create :749 (webhook scope when the trigger is WEBHOOK), update/delete/setActive through findWritableRule (:414-419, which adds the webhook scope for WEBHOOK rules), reorder :903, rotate :931, regenerate :967, runNow :986, resetToDefaults :1031. create, rotate, regenerate and runNow also pass sensitiveProcedure at 10/min (:144-152). UI: AutomationRuleList.tsx:178-180 locks the switch, Edit and Delete on WEBHOOK rules when !canManageWebhooks. canManageWebhooks comes from the server (router:718).

checks.name: tenant scoping of every automation query and of task.list/getById/getByEntity (owner ruling 6)
checks.evidence: Every router query filters by ctx.tenant.tenantId (router:398-405, 582, 598, 698-708, 728, 764, 819-835, 852-854, 871-889, 905-921, 941, 947, 971). Store tenant filters are at store.ts:294, 450, 458, 471, 479, 486, 492, 585, 632, 643, 657, 665, and the admission advisory lock is per tenant (:275-278). task.router.ts:206-213 withAssigneeVisibility narrows non-admins to owner OR assignee. It is applied to list (taskListWhere :226-234), getById (:318-321) and, new in e6f678441, getByEntity (:981-984). The task.router.test.ts case asserts the `{leadId, tenantId, AND:[{OR:[{ownerId},{assigneeId}]}]}` shape.

checks.name: notification links do not point recipients at tasks they cannot open
checks.evidence: task-automation-engine.ts:755-763 sets canOpenTask = userId === ownerId || userId === assigneeId, where assigneeId is null when assignment failed (:728-731), which errs on the side of not linking. task-automation-runtime.ts notificationLink returns the deep link /tasks/<id> plus entityId only when canOpenTask is true, /tasks otherwise, and /tasks/automation for failure notices. createTaskAutomationRuntime spreads notificationLink(request) into createNotification. The test 'links the task only for recipients who can open it' covers owner, assignee and a third user.

checks.name: link-fallback fix (uncommitted) creates no orphan tasks and hides no failures
checks.evidence: In `git diff`: task-automation-engine.ts:619 now retries unlinked only when created.linkRejected is true. runtime toCreateTaskResult sets linkRejected only when error.reason === 'TASK_LINK_REJECTED'. TaskService.ts assignmentError (lines 33-36) returns TaskLinkRejectedError only when the validation result is not checkFailed. checkFailed is set for an unknown entity type and for a lookup that throws (TaskService.ts:846-861). Not found, malformed id, converted lead and closed opportunity (:866-919) are link rejections. TaskLinkRejectedError (ApplicationErrors.ts) extends ValidationError, so the code, message and tRPC mapping are unchanged. Every refusal happens before the save, so a rejected linked create persisted nothing and the unlinked retry cannot duplicate it. A PersistenceError carries no reason, so it fails the run. The new engine test asserts that a 'Failed to save task' produces exactly one create attempt and status FAILED with errorCode task_create_failed.

checks.name: run-history retention (privacy)
checks.evidence: engine.ts:812-822 purges runs older than L.runRetentionDays in batches and keeps purgeBacklog set until a short batch shows it has caught up (456c86583). store.ts:688-700 purges terminal runs (SUCCEEDED/FAILED/SKIPPED, :245). reapStaleRuns (:673-676) turns stuck RUNNING runs into FAILED so they become purgeable. Stored webhook context is limited to template-referenced own scalar keys, capped in length and count (webhook.ts:190-211). listRuns returns no context or payload (router:731-740).

findings.scenario: In production TASK_AUTOMATION_INTERVAL_MS=0, so the tick that claims, reaps and purges runs never runs, but the webhook route is still mounted unconditionally. A tenant that enables automation and creates a webhook rule can have runs admitted (202). Those runs stay PENDING with their webhook context (capped scalar payload values) and are never purged, because purgeRunsBefore (task-automation-store.ts:688-700) only removes terminal statuses and only runs from the tick. Per-rule and per-tenant hourly caps bound the volume. Automation being off in production is accepted until #966, so this is a retention note, not a blocker.
findings.fix: While the runner interval is 0, answer the webhook route with the same 503 'unavailable' used for missing encryption (or 404), or let purge/expiry cover non-terminal runs older than the retention window. Alternatively, record this on PG-208-AUTOMATION-OFF-IN-PROD-001 so the outbox move (#966) closes it.

findings.scenario: canOpenTask is true only for the task owner and the assignee. An admin or a manager whose team scope covers the task's owner can open the task, but gets the generic /tasks link. This errs on the safe side (no wrong deep links, no information leak) and is only a UX gap, consistent with the accepted PG-208-ASSIGNEE-REMINDERS-001 scope.
findings.fix: Optional: resolve visibility through the same predicate as task.getById (role-aware) before choosing the link. No security change is needed.
